criteria.text: When the runtime confirms a busy check never started, I can keep waiting without a fixed attempt limit, with at least 10 seconds between busy uploads and any longer server delay respected.
When Check capacity is usable and full, my next upload waits for a free Check slot or 60 seconds from the busy answer, while still respecting the minimum delay.
If capacity information is unsupported, absent or unusable, my check can try again after the minimum delay without treating missing information as free capacity.
A deadline, Ctrl-C, maintenance or an access refusal prevents further uploads even when the capacity hold would otherwise end.
Reading or explicitly retrying my saved batch preserves the original retry times, selected files, request history and call limits.
A check that may have started is recovered by its original request ID and is never replayed as a busy check.

cases.given: An agent Check has its 90-second caller wait, immediate passed lint, unsupported capacity 404 and repeated confirmed-unstarted complete zero-call busy receipts; each busy reply advises Retry-After 1 second.
cases.required_observation: More than 3 and at most 10 actual Check uploads before the finite deadline; consecutive busy uploads are at least 10000 ms apart and none begins at/after deadline. Preserve all posted request IDs/raw receipts; end busy/not-run exit 5 with zero Check calls and existing advice. No per-attempt Check ID, dispatch claim or archive upload while only waiting; no global attempt-count cap.

cases.given: Unsupported capacity 404; four confirmed-unstarted complete zero-call busy receipts with Retry-After 1 second, then a matching passed check receipt; caller wait 90 seconds and identical source/call ceilings throughout.
cases.required_observation: The fifth Check POST can succeed after at least 40000 ms of busy waits and before deadline; preserve all five POST identities and receipts, matching final usage and original ceilings. Continue beyond three attempts without allocating an ID for mere waiting.

cases.given: A confirmed-unstarted busy Check answer arrives at time 0 with Retry-After 75 seconds; usable Check occupancy remains full; caller deadline 90000 ms.
cases.required_observation: No new Check ID/claim/upload before 75000 ms, including at the 60000 ms capacity bound. After 75000 ms ordinary guarded admission may send one fresh Check attempt despite continued full occupancy; preserve prior evidence.

cases.given: Busy answer at time 0 advises 1 second; usable Check running/limit counts remain 4/4 through minimum wait, then an eligible shared capacity observation at 30000 ms reports 3/4; caller wait 90 seconds.
cases.required_observation: No replacement upload while observed full before 30000 ms; after minimum wait and the observed free slot, ordinary guarded admission can dispatch before 60000 ms. Use small authenticated GETs/cache outside local claims, without extra attempt IDs or archive uploads just to wait.

cases.given: Busy answer at time 0 advises 1 second; usable Check occupancy stays 4/4 throughout; finite wait 90 seconds and all other gates permit dispatch.
cases.required_observation: No replacement upload before 60000 ms; at the 60000 ms hold bound ordinary guarded admission may resume without requiring a free count. Minimum backoff remains satisfied; do not reset the bound at each capacity observation.

cases.given: Busy answer at time 0 advises 1 second; supported Check occupancy remains running 0/limit 0; all other gates permit dispatch within 90 seconds.
cases.required_observation: Treat limit 0 as full rather than free: no replacement upload until 60000 ms capacity bound; ordinary guards still apply at that bound.

cases.given: Separately capacity 404, a recognized non-maintenance response with absent Check occupancy, malformed Check counts and an unclear capacity read; busy answer at time 0 advises 1 second, caller wait 90 seconds.
cases.required_observation: Missing/unusable data supplies no free count or new hard refusal. Existing unsupported/warning/fail-open behavior permits ordinary guarded Check admission after at least 10000 ms; unclear results share the existing cache scope/TTL and finite per-command warning behavior. No exact GET count is required.

cases.given: A confirmed busy answer at time 0 advises 1 second and caller deadline is 9000 ms; repeat with usable full occupancy and caller deadline 45000 ms.
cases.required_observation: The minimum wait or full-capacity hold reaches the caller deadline without a replacement Check ID, claim or POST. Preserve earlier receipts, zero Check usage and existing busy/not-run exit 5; allocate/send nothing afterward.

cases.given: Busy Check answer at time 0 advises 1 second, usable occupancy stays full; Ctrl-C at 15000 ms before deadline and capacity bound.
cases.required_observation: No replacement Check ID/claim/upload; retain earlier IDs/confirmed receipts and uncertain unrelated leases. Existing Check exit 3 and valid JSON remain; text says Stopped. with what was sent/confirmed, not wait-ended or Stopped before sending. for the posted attempt.

cases.given: Busy Check answer at time 0 advises 1 second; a supported capacity observation then announces maintenance until 120000 ms. Caller deadline 90000 ms, so the 60000 ms capacity bound falls inside maintenance.
cases.required_observation: No replacement Check ID/claim/upload at 60000 ms or before caller deadline. Respect bounded maintenance waits/local-time notice and existing exit/accounting; capacity fallback cannot bypass maintenance.

cases.given: During a confirmed-busy Check capacity wait, shared observation returns recognized 401, no-cloud-access, not-invited, cloud-unavailable or update-required separately before the hold ends.
cases.required_observation: Apply the existing matching stop behavior and exit/advice, preserving earlier evidence; no capacity-fallback replacement, archive upload or new Check ID. Do not turn an access stop into unclear fail-open.

cases.given: Busy answer at time 0 advises 1 second and usable occupancy stays full. First invocation is interrupted at 5000 ms; read at 7000 ms, then explicitly retry at 20000 ms with identical owner/repo/source/caps and a wait ending after 60000 ms. Separately retry at 8000 ms with unsupported capacity 404, and repeat with Retry-After 75 seconds.
cases.required_observation: GET-only read creates no attempt and preserves the original 10000 ms minimum and 60000 ms capacity bound. Full-capacity retry may dispatch after 60000 ms under ordinary guards rather than starting another 60 seconds; the unsupported variant waits the remaining minimum until 10000 ms, and the 75 second variant cannot dispatch before 75000 ms. All prior IDs/receipts and original source/caps remain intact.

cases.given: Separately a lost POST reply, wrong-ID/command receipt, unknown/positive calls, evaluated checks, incomplete accounting and expired/unverifiable evidence; capacity later shows a free slot or 60000 ms passes.
cases.required_observation: No capacity replacement or fresh request ID regardless of elapsed time/free capacity. Recover accepted/uncertain submissions by their original IDs under existing lifecycle, retain unknown/known accounting and paid leases, and preserve the separately authorized restart exception without broadening it.

cases.given: An older saved authoritative complete zero-call confirmed-unstarted busy receipt has no new minimum/capacity timestamps. At first batch read at time 20000 ms it has a shorter valid saved retry_at; repeat with a longer saved retry_at of 95000 ms. A later retry at 40000 ms observes usable full occupancy; repeat read/retry after that. Separately use a never-posted held row with passed lint and no busy proof.
cases.required_observation: The first new-format batch operation saves minimum at least 30000 ms (or 95000 ms when that saved wait is longer) and capacity bound 80000 ms. Later read/retry preserves those anchors without another 60 second restart; full occupancy may release ordinary guarded dispatch at 80000 ms, but the longer-wait variant cannot dispatch before 95000 ms. No timestamp is guessed from sent_at, no ID/usage/eligibility is invented, and UUID-only reads do not rewrite the batch. The never-posted held row keeps existing first-send eligibility without a busy cooldown.
